methods.label: Check the conditions and interpretation
methods.explanation:
If each choice is checked as a complete statement without assuming that all lines lie in one plane, A is the intended answer.

The parallel postulate emphasizes “a point outside the line”; parallel lines must lie in the same plane; two lines parallel to the same line are parallel to each other, not perpendicular.

C fails when the point lies on the given line: every line through that point shares a point with the given line and therefore cannot be parallel to it. In B, without a common-plane assumption, two lines can have no common point yet fail to lie in the same plane, so they need not be parallel. If all lines are assumed to lie in one plane, however, B is also true. Thus A is the intended choice under the first interpretation, while both A and B are correct under the plane-only interpretation; the wording is ambiguous.
methods.levelReason: The explanation uses Grade 7 parallel-line definitions, the parallel postulate and its corollary, together with the elementary definition of perpendicularity. The coplanarity clarification requires no spatial calculations or advanced theorem.
